nodes.description: Recipient proteins do not receive their clusters. Two consequences matter in the erythroblast: iron regulatory protein 1 stays in its cluster-free RNA-binding form, and ferrochelatase, itself a cluster enzyme, loses activity. Both were established for this pathway rather than specifically in HSPA9 patient erythroblasts.

nodes.description: Iron keeps arriving at the erythroblast mitochondrion but cannot be put into heme, so it accumulates in the perinuclear ring that defines the sideroblastic anemias. The review's reading is that in iron-sulfur cluster defects the ring is not a direct mitochondrial iron-handling fault but a consequence of the iron-sensing and heme-synthesis block above it.

evidence.reference_title: The molecular genetics of sideroblastic anemia.
evidence.snippet: The sideroblastic anemias (SAs) are a group of inherited and acquired bone marrow disorders defined by pathological iron accumulation in the mitochondria of erythroid precursors.

evidence.reference_title: Congenital sideroblastic anemia due to mutations in the mitochondrial HSP70 homologue HSPA9.
evidence.snippet: Here we demonstrate that mutations in HSPA9, a mitochondrial HSP70 homolog located in the chromosome 5q deletion syndrome 5q33 critical deletion interval and involved in mitochondrial Fe-S biogenesis, result in CSA inherited as an autosomal recessive trait.

nodes.description: Heterozygotes are viable with half-normal Hspa9 expression, have normal basal haematopoiesis and do not develop myelodysplastic syndrome, but show a cell-intrinsic B-progenitor colony defect. Homozygotes die as embryos.

HSPA9 works with the co-chaperone HSCB to move the newly built [2Fe-2S] cluster off the ISCU scaffold and onto glutaredoxin 5, which then distributes it to recipient proteins. This is the rate-limiting step of the disease, and it is distinct from the assembly step of the MMDS genes and from the export step of ABCB7: synthesis on the scaffold still happens, but the cluster cannot be handed on. Disease variants in HSPA9, HSCB and GLRX5 all converge on it, which is why the three genes cause the same anemia.

nodes.description: A common coding single nucleotide polymorphism that lowers HSPA9 messenger RNA expression. On its own it causes no disease, and it is frequent in the population; in trans with a severe allele it lowers total chaperone dosage below the threshold at which erythropoiesis fails. It is the second hit that makes an otherwise recessive disease look dominant. Whether the polymorphism itself lowers expression or merely marks a linked causal variant is unsettled.

evidence.reference_title: Congenital sideroblastic anemia due to mutations in the mitochondrial HSP70 homologue HSPA9.
evidence.snippet: a common coding single nucleotide polymorphism in trans that correlates with reduced messenger RNA expression

nodes.description: Microcytic anemia in many patients, though others are normocytic, so red-cell indices do not exclude the diagnosis.

A subset of patients is transfusion-dependent, at the severe end of a range that runs from mild and transfusion-independent. Transfusion is supportive: no therapy addresses the chaperone deficit, and the dosage that sets severity is fixed at conception.

Total functional HSPA9 falls below the level erythropoiesis requires. Dosage, rather than any single allele, sets severity: a severe allele with a hypomorph gives the clinical phenotype while a severe allele with a normally expressed one often does not. Complete absence is not survivable, as homozygous knockout is embryonic lethal in the mouse.

evidence.reference_title: Reduced levels of Hspa9 attenuate Stat5 activation in mouse B cells.
evidence.snippet: Although homozygous knockout of Hspa9 is embryonically lethal, mice with heterozygous deletion of Hspa9 (Hspa9(+/-)) are viable and have a 50% reduction in Hspa9 expression.

nodes.description: A germline HSPA9 allele that abolishes or nearly abolishes function: nonsense, frameshift, an in-frame deletion that behaves as a null in yeast complementation, or a splice-region change. One de novo missense allele in the nucleotide-binding region has also been reported. No patient is homozygous for two such alleles.

nodes.description: Cluster-free iron regulatory protein 1 binds the iron-responsive element in the 5-prime untranslated region of the erythroid ALAS2 message and blocks its translation. ALAS2 catalyses the first and rate-limiting step of heme synthesis, so the cell behaves as though iron-starved while iron is in fact plentiful. This step is carried over from the glutaredoxin 5 model of the same pathway and has not been shown in HSPA9 patient cells.

evidence.reference_title: Deficiency of glutaredoxin 5 reveals Fe-S clusters are required for vertebrate haem synthesis.
evidence.snippet: We found that loss of Fe-S cluster assembly in sir animals activated IRP1 and blocked haem biosynthesis catalysed by aminolaevulinate synthase 2 (ALAS2).

evidence.reference_title: Deficiency of glutaredoxin 5 reveals Fe-S clusters are required for vertebrate haem synthesis.
evidence.snippet: Overexpression of ALAS2 RNA without the 5' iron response element that binds IRP1 rescued sir embryos, whereas overexpression of ALAS2 including the iron response element did not.
